plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A hardy evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green leaves and nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that age to pinkish tones. It is prized for flowering in the depths of winter, often pushing through snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to late winter (December to February in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mountain woodlands of central and southern Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a rose but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic.

plants.name: Hamamelis mollis
plants.description: A deciduous large shrub or small tree that produces spidery, strongly fragrant flowers with ribbon-like petals on bare branches. The flowers curl up in freezing temperatures to protect themselves and unfurl again when it warms.
plants.location: Central and eastern China; cultivated in temperate gardens across Europe, North America and Japan
plants.funFact: Witch hazel flowers can survive hard freezes by curling their petals into tight spirals and reopening when conditions improve.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tree with fern-like leaves that bursts into masses of vivid scarlet-orange flowers. In some regions of the Southern Hemisphere and tropics it flowers around the turn of the year.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February); varies by tropical region
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in Australia, southern Africa, the Caribbean, India and tropical regions worldwide
plants.funFact: It is native to only a small area of Madagascar and is endangered in the wild, yet it is one of the most widely planted ornamental trees in the tropics.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and large, rose-like blooms. In mild climates it provides rich color in the middle of winter when few other shrubs are flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring (December to April)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and China; cultivated in the southeastern United States, the Pacific Northwest, Europe and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of Camellia sinensis, the plant from which all true tea is made.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with strap-like leaves and tall stalks topped with rounded clusters of trumpet-shaped blue flowers. It thrives in summer heat and blooms around the new year in the Southern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (December to February in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South Africa; naturalized and cultivated in Australia, New Zealand and Mediterranean-climate regions
plants.funFact: Its name comes from the Greek words agape (love) and anthos (flower), although it is not a true lily.
